To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

“Daily rhythms of activity and mRNA abundance for enzymes involved in glucose metabolism in liver persist even in the absence (constant darkness and food deprivation) of both environmental cues (light and food), suggesting that the endogenous circadian system plays a major role in their regulation”.

(a) daily rhythms of mRNA abundance and enzyme activities in liver are well defined and persist even in the absence or food and/or light; (b) the light–dark and the feeding cycles influence such rhythms; and (c) cortisol is not the main factor involved in the generation of such rhythms.

“In rainbow trout, daily rhythms in the mRNA levels of enzymes involved in carbohydrate and lipid metabolism persist under conditions of constant darkness or food deprivation, indicating the endogenous and metabolic nature of such rhythms.”
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of the daily variations of several key enzymes involved in the metabolism of glucose and lipids in rainbow trout liver.

a model of teleoest fish that reveals the existence of daily rhythms in liver metabolism that are not only influenced by the presence of food but are also dependent on light/dark cycle, and that are not mainly mediated by the hypothalamo–pituitary–interrenal axis.
the existence of daily variations of activity and/or mRNA abundance of enzymes and genes involved in glucose and fatty acid metabolism in liver of a teleost fish.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

daily rhythms in the activity and mRNA abundance in liver of rainbow trouts of the analysed enzymes involved in major pathways related to glucose and lipid metabolism are mainly endogenous and are influenced by food availability, and to a lesser extent, also by the light/darkness cycle.
in rainbow trout the light/dark and feeding time cycles are not essential to maintain the endogenous daily rhythms of liver enzymes involved in carbohydrate and lipid metabolism.

the circadian clock in rainbow trout liver seems to be mainly involved on the regulation of the daily rhythms of the enzymes involved in carbohydrate metabolism, whereas the rhythms of lipid metabolism seem to be mainly dependent on food availability.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the daily changes in activity of key enzymes of carbohydrate and lipid metabolisms in rainbow trout liver are mainly driven by daily variations in the availability of food.

the light/dark and feeding cycles are important in regulating the activity and expression of genes involved in carbohydrate and lipid metabolism, and that the daily rhythms in gene expression are likely to be involved in generating the daily rhythms in enzyme activity.

daily changes in activity of key proteins of carbohydrate and lipid metabolisms in liver are mainly driven by endogenous rhythms, and that the light/dark and food availability are important modulators of such endogenous rhythms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the liver of fish is a highly dynamic organ, and its metabolism undergoes important changes throughout the day.
the daily rhythms observed in liver of fish are not only related to food intake but are also influenced by the light/dark rhythm, suggesting the existence of a circadian regulation.

, in the absence of food, the liver of fish is capable of maintaining its metabolic activity, and the daily variations of the activity and mRNA abundance are mainly driven by the light–dark cycles, which are also able to influence the rhythms in liver metabolism.
